tests: teardown --from-reconstructed gives up on a remote that never answers

consumesExternalOutput.program: git ls-remote --symref <remote> HEAD, against a TCP listener that accepts and never speaks
consumesExternalOutput.provenance: src/pool.ts spawns this command, so SPAWN_GREP matches and rule (f) binds, and the property the bound exists for is a property of git rather than of this kernel: git imposes no wait of its own. The capture records that measured at two different waits on 2026-09-16 against git 2.43.0, exit 124 and empty output both times, so the reader can see the second is not a longer version of a timeout that had already fired. The named test reads the capture and asserts it still shows the unbounded wait before exercising the bound. The two dangerous states are structurally different: the first removes the BOUND so the command runs unbounded again, the second leaves the bound and removes the DIAGNOSIS, so the refusal arrives but says `Error: spawnSync git ETIMEDOUT` instead of naming the wait, which is the version an operator cannot act on.
